cards.b: Production: total output made. Productivity: efficiency of inputs, e.g. output per worker.
Output in a time period ÷ number of employees.
Training, better motivation, automation, quality control to cut waste, lean production, better inventory management.

cards.f: Problems of holding too much inventory
cards.b: High storage and insurance costs, cash tied up, risk of waste, damage, theft or going out of date.

cards.f: Problems of holding too little inventory
cards.b: Production may stop, orders unmet (lost sales), no bulk-buying discounts.
Minimum inventory kept for emergencies such as late delivery or sudden demand.
Buffer inventory + (daily usage × lead time). Lead time = time between ordering and delivery.
Techniques that reduce waste (time, materials, movement, inventory, faults) and raise efficiency.
Continuous improvement through small, frequent changes suggested by workers, often in teams.
Little or no inventory held; materials arrive as needed. Saves storage and cash, but needs reliable suppliers.
Production line split into cells, each team making a complete part. Improves teamworking and multi-skilling.
Job: one product to order. Batch: group of identical products, then switch. Flow: continuous, large-scale production line.
Very high set-up cost, boring repetitive work, one breakdown stops the line, no variety.
Control: checking at the end of production. Assurance: standards agreed and checked throughout the process.
Every employee is responsible for quality and customer satisfaction at each stage, including the next worker in the process.

short.q: Calculate the labour productivity of a factory with 50 workers producing 6,500 units a week. [2]
Maximum inventory is 1,000 units, buffer is 200 units, usage is 100 units per day and lead time is 2 days. Calculate the re-order level. [2]
Explain one advantage and one risk of using just-in-time production. [4]
short.model: Advantage: little inventory is held, so storage costs fall and less cash is tied up. Risk: a late delivery from a supplier stops production.
points: advantage: lower storage costs/cash tied up

short.q: Explain why flow production is not suitable for a business making hand-made wedding dresses. [3]
short.model: Each dress is unique and made to order, so job production is needed. Flow production suits identical products in large quantities and has very high set-up costs.
points: high set-up cost would not be justified

short.q: Distinguish between quality control and quality assurance. [3]
short.model: Quality control checks products at the end of production. Quality assurance sets standards and checks them at every stage, so faults are found earlier and waste is lower.
